auditFailuresRepaired: stops.all-answered (audit run 1) -> the S1 entry was written exactly as the prompt's mechanized-human rule specifies, `- status: RESOLVED-IN-ARM (agent-maintainer, 2026-08-03) · resolved-in-arm (...)`. Root cause is a real toolkit inconsistency, not a mistake in the entry: `RESOLVED-IN-ARM` is a first-class state in the RENDERER (render.py `_parse_status` and decision-entry.schema.json both list it) but classify.py's `parse_ledger` computes `answered` with `re.search(r'-\s*status:\s*ANSWERED', block)`, so RESOLVED-IN-ARM reads as unanswered everywhere the classifier looks — the audit's stop gate, MR-3 stop satisfaction, and Stage-D pending-stop absorption. The renderer parses the head as ANSWERED (so lifecycle status advances to Approved) and the trailing segments are preserved verbatim; the classifier now counts it answered.
